Structural entropy vs redundancy (measured)

          
Reading the profile
H is the Shannon entropy of a grammar's construct histogram (bits): how evenly its surface forms spread across a universal construct taxonomy. Redundancy = 1 − H/log2(C) is the surface variety that is syntactic sugar rather than free information. Surface/construct = N/C is the mean number of surface forms per universal construct — the distance a universal IR must collapse for that language. These are grammar-derived (structural) measures, not corpus frequencies.

          
The information-theoretic frame used throughout: I = H_task − H_corpus → 0. Once a competence is admitted by replay, each act costs a lookup floor (~1 µJ) rather than a cold proposal (~5,000,000 µJ). The frame is a hypothesis priced in joules, not a settled law.

Who builds language ontologies, universal IRs, and cross-language translators — surveyed globally, credited where more mature. This artifact is a measurement and navigation layer over that existing work; it does not claim to replace it.

        

        
Where this artifact sits

        
Curation efforts (Linguist, PLDB, Acher's merged catalog, Rosetta Code, Hyperpolyglot) enumerate languages and evidence. Grammar efforts (tree-sitter, ANTLR grammars-v4) make syntax machine-readable. Code ontologies (srcML, Kythe, Glean, Semantic, SCIP/LSIF) index facts about code across languages. Universal IRs (LLVM, MLIR, WebAssembly, JVM/CIL, GraalVM/Truffle) and cross-language compilers (Haxe, py2many, c2rust, CrossTL, RIKEN Omni) lower or translate between languages. What is measured here is the per-language surface-to-construct distance and the construct bridge between any two measured languages, with an explicit honesty contract: unmeasured languages carry no invented numbers. The replay-gated, joule-priced admission layer is the part not covered by the surveyed peers; it is stated as a hypothesis under test, not as a marketed conclusion.

      


      

        
Provenance of the 12,119-language universe: a merge of public curation efforts, each counted below. A language's badge set shows which efforts record it; measurement (a real grammar ingested) is a separate, stricter claim.

        

        
Honesty contract
Curated ≠ measured. 60 languages have a real tree-sitter grammar ingested and 100% named-node coverage; the rest are present as catalogued nodes with no invented entropy or coverage. Mercury is excluded because its public grammar is a one-node stub. Structural entropy is labelled structural and never conflated with corpus entropy.

      

      

        
How a language enters an editor ecosystem. Three packaging standards, converging on shared open artifacts: a grammar, a language server (LSP), a debug adapter (DAP), and a per-ecosystem manifest. LSP/DAP amortize semantics across ecosystems; the grammar and packaging remain per-ecosystem — the residual impedance tax.

Global editor ecosystems — the mechanism each exposes
EcosystemOriginGrammar / syntaxSemanticsDebugPackaging / extension standard

        
Reading
Rust, Go, Python and Zig each reached all three ecosystems by supplying the same logical bundle — grammar, language server, debug adapter, manifest — but re-packaged per ecosystem. rust-analyzer, gopls, pyright/Pylance and zls are LSP servers reused across VSCode and Zed (and via LSP API in IntelliJ); the grammar is re-expressed as TextMate vs tree-sitter vs PSI, and the manifest as package.json vs extension.toml vs plugin.xml. The semantics amortize; the syntax and packaging do not. That per-ecosystem re-expression is the impedance tax a universal construct IR plus generated adapters targets.

      

      

        
Two different axes: immersion (how deeply an editor surfaces a language: grammar → semantic tokens/inlays → completion → navigation → refactor/code actions → diagnostics → debug → live/REPL → AI context) and competence (whether what the editor surfaces is verified, replay-admitted, content-addressed and costed). Most languages are stale or absent on immersion; essentially none are competence-backed. The exemplar of competence immersed live is rust-analyzer + the borrow checker: a gate surfaced as inline diagnostics/inlays so violations appear at edit time, not debug time.

The gap and the unlock (hypothesis)

        
Immersion adapters are hand-maintained per ecosystem, so they drift from changing editor specs or are never built — the staleness gap. Competence-backed immersion exists only as per-language, hand-built proofs-of-concept (Lean infoview goal/type at cursor; Agda/Idris hole-driven editing where the editor requests a verified term; Unison's content-addressed, type-checked-by-hash codebase; Smalltalk/Pharo live images; Light Table / Bret Victor immediate feedback; MPS projectional editing). None is universal, generated, or joule-costed.

        
The proposed unlock: represent every language by one universal construct IR; generate the immersion adapters (grammar, queries, LSP, DAP, manifest) from it so they cannot go stale; and back editor features with admitted competence (replay-verified, content-addressed, joule-priced handlers). Then diagnostics become admission failures caught at edit time, debugging becomes replay-divergence localized to a construct, and completion becomes admitted competence rather than a heuristic guess. Errors and debugging trend toward zero because known-correct handlers replace re-derived code and every edit is gated before use. This is stated as a hypothesis under test, not a delivered claim.

      

      

        
The true view of language usability: a language is only as maintainable as its living tooling. This table organizes measured languages by grammar maintenance (active = pushed <1 yr; stale = 1–3 yr; dormant = >3 yr; dead = archived), with tree-sitter grammar repo, LSP and debug-adapter availability. Legacy-infrastructure languages (COBOL, Fortran, PL/I, RPG, Pascal) are included deliberately — critical code that still needs experts. Maintenance is probed deterministically from GitHub repo metadata, not guessed.

The computation stack as a domain blueprint — intent → meaning → code → compiler → silicon → verified reuse. These are independent, for-purpose layers, not the ad-hoc "make-build-fix" loop today's ecosystems are stuck in. Three structures make a universal, deterministic substrate possible: an ontology (shared meaning), a taxonomy (compression), and a knowledge graph with a verification gate (robust reuse). This page is the blueprint and the evidence for why such a substrate is feasible and how its robustness is ensured — a neutral reference, not a product pitch.

        

          
1 · INTENT
A human goal, in natural language or a spec. A formal, parseable specification bridges intent to meaning. A proposer — human or machine — suggests; a gate admits. (Spec-driven design globally points at this bridge; the open problem is making it deterministic rather than re-interpreted each time.)

          
▼ ontology fixes meaning

          
2 · MEANING — a universal IR
An ontology of computation: content-addressed, name-free intended models (Gruber 1993 / Guarino 1998 — an explicit specification of a conceptualization). A finite construct vocabulary is the taxonomy: the basic-level / minimum-description-length code over operations (Rosch; Corter & Gluck 1992, category utility). Evidence: 104 languages measured at 100% named-node coverage onto 113 constructs; surface redundancy 0.10–0.26 — the surfaces really do compress onto a shared code.

          
▼ taxonomy compresses (encoder / decoder)

          
3 · CODE — target surfaces
Rust / Python / COBOL / Verilog / … — one meaning, many surfaces. Lookup-table encoders/decoders map construct↔surface; emission covers every ingested language. Description length collapses onto the shared taxonomy rather than being re-derived per language.

          
▼

          
4 · COMPILER → ASSEMBLY
Lowering meaning to machine code (ARM64 / x86-64 / …). Optimization is capability-derived: a fused multiply-add is emitted iff the fabric has it — the bolt-on "flags" become a lookup, removing the curse of ignorance (accidental flag knowledge gating peak performance). Evidence: emitted code byte-exact against the system toolchain and meaning-checked on real silicon. Infrastructure peers (LLVM, MLIR, Mojo/MAX) unify compiler detail; a meaning layer sits above them.

          
▼

          
5 · SILICON / FABRIC
CPU / GPU / NPU / quantum / thermodynamic / spatial / neuromorphic / analog — the costed primitive floor. Hundreds of compilers and dozens of IRs/VMs/OSes all lower to this same small floor: diversity is surface (high entropy), the floor is shared (low entropy). Execution returns a measured joule receipt (µJ per act).

          
▼ verification gate = a mechanism / costly signal

          
6 · VERIFIED REUSE — a gated knowledge graph
A knowledge graph admits a node/edge only by reproducing its examples — a costly signal that makes truth-telling the dominant strategy (mechanism design for ontology alignment). Admitted competence is content-addressed and joule-priced, so reuse is a lookup at the energy floor rather than re-derivation by an expensive proposer. This is the robustness guarantee: nothing enters the shared catalog unverified.

          
↺ feedback: admitted competence → cheap lookup → cheaper next act

        

        
The three structures, one stack

          
Ontologyshared meaning — a prior / compression scheme

          
Taxonomyfinite construct code — MDL / basic level

          
Knowledge graph + gateverified, costed reuse — a coordination mechanism

          
Global roots credited: Gruber/Guarino formal ontology; Rosch/Corter-Gluck basic-level information; Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika seven padārthas and Buddhist Abhidharma (finite explicit category systems, ~2000 yr); mechanism design for ontology alignment. The information/game-theory readings are interpretive lenses grounded in cited work; a formal MDL-optimality proof of the construct count is open. The measurements above are the evidence that a universal, deterministic coding substrate is feasible and can be made robust — independent of any single implementation of it.

Every edit is replay-gated before it is served; errors are caught at edit time; debugging is replay-divergence, not post-hoc. These are measured prototype receipts, not a delivered product claim.

Generated adapters

What this tests
Zero-error hypothesis: because nothing is served unless it replays every probe, errors cannot escape to runtime (escaped_errors = 0) and post-hoc debug sessions are 0; reuse lowers cost per act toward the lookup floor. Native-language synthesis turns each fabric capability-gap into a language-as-data (constructs + seed grammar + emission LUT + declared native semantics); production lowering to the fabric remains open.
